findings.title: Team permission check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which is only true for a user who is both admin and owner. Despite the name, team admins (and in most role models, owners who are not reported as admins) will be denied and get FORBIDDEN. It should be `||`. Additionally, when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is null, `?? 0` queries a non-existent team on every personal booking — two wasted DB round trips.

findings.title: Duplicate guest emails within the request are not de-duplicated server-side
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters emails that already exist as attendees; it does not remove duplicates inside the incoming `guests` array, and the trpc schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) does not enforce uniqueness. Uniqueness is only validated in the client dialog, so any other caller (or a crafted request) can create several attendee rows with the same email on one booking, resulting in duplicated calendar attendees and duplicated emails.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side, allowing bypass
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but the incoming guest email is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A guest email with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@x.com`) bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS protection. Lowercase the guest email before comparison. The existing-attendee comparison is similarly case-sensitive, so `Foo@x.com` can be added when `foo@x.com` is already an attendee.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input list instead of the actually added guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input. In email-manager the list decides who receives the full "scheduled" email vs the "guests added" notice, so any email that was filtered out (already an attendee, or blacklisted) will incorrectly receive a brand-new booking confirmation email. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed without the error details
findings.body: The catch block logs a fixed string via `console.log` and discards `err`, so email delivery/render failures for this new flow are effectively invisible in production. Use the project logger and include the error and bookingId.

findings.title: No restriction on booking state; any attendee can add guests to any booking
findings.body: The handler permits the action when the caller is simply one of the booking's attendees, with no check that the booking is ACCEPTED/not cancelled and not in the past, and no check for seated events (`seatsPerTimeSlot`). Adding attendees to a cancelled/past booking sends out CONFIRMED ICS invites, and adding guests to a seats-based event bypasses the seat accounting.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports from its own package barrel, creating a circular import
findings.body: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports `MultiEmail` (via MultiEmailLazy). This module cycle can yield undefined components at runtime depending on evaluation order/bundler. Import the components from their concrete paths (e.g. `../components/button`, `../components/form`) as the sibling form components do.

findings.title: Add button silently does nothing when all email rows are removed
findings.body: `handleAdd` returns early when `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, with no toast or validation message, so after removing every row the Add button appears unresponsive. Also, the initial value is `[""]`, so pressing Add immediately validates an empty string and shows "Emails must be unique and valid" rather than a clearer empty-input message.

findings.title: "Add guests" action id/label mismatch and shown for past bookings
findings.body: The new action uses `id: "add_members"` with label `t("additional_guests")`, which is inconsistent and makes the test id (`add_members`) misleading. More importantly, `editBookingActions` is also rendered for past and pending bookings (lines 553-554), so users are offered "add guests" on bookings that already happened, which triggers new CONFIRMED invite emails for a past event.

findings.title: Organizer email subject can render "undefined"/empty name
findings.body: The subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. Newly added guests are created with `name: ""`, and if attendee ordering places a new guest first the subject becomes "Guests Added:  with  at ...". It also throws if `attendees` is empty. Fall back to the booker name/email as other organizer templates do.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: This PR adds a new mutation that mutates booking attendees, updates external calendars and sends emails, with non-trivial authorization and filtering logic (team admin/owner check, blacklist, dedupe). No unit or e2e tests are included, so regressions in the permission check or the filtering cannot be caught.
